Wind and solar beat coal for the first time
Coal output hits a record low

explanation.summary: Where US electricity comes from, month by month. Coal was the backbone of the grid in 2008. Cheap natural gas took first place in 2016, and wind and solar have since passed coal too. Nuclear stayed steady the whole time.
explanation.methodology: Net generation by fuel for all sectors from EIA electric power operational data (EIA API), in billion kWh per month: coal, natural gas, nuclear, and wind plus solar.

key_findings.title: 2008: Coal Rules
key_findings.description: Coal produced 48% of US electricity in 2008; natural gas produced 21%.
key_findings.significance: Almost half the grid ran on coal.

key_findings.title: 2016: Gas Takes First Place
key_findings.description: Cheap shale gas made gas plants cheaper to run. In 2016 gas produced 34% of US power and coal 30%, the first full year gas led.
key_findings.significance: Market prices, more than rules, pushed coal down.

key_findings.title: April 2022: Wind and Solar Pass Coal
key_findings.description: For the first time, wind and solar produced more power than coal in a single month. In 2024 they passed coal for the whole year. In 2025 coal supplied 16.6% and gas 40.8%.
key_findings.significance: Coal's share fell by about two thirds in 17 years.
